pr_title: Fix stack overflow condition when appending modifiers to resolver chains.

issue_context.title: [System.Text.Json] Stack Overflow when appending modifiers to TypeInfoResolverChain
issue_context.body:
The code 

```C#
using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata;

JsonSerializerOptions options = new(JsonSerializerOptions.Default);
options.TypeInfoResolverChain.Add(new DefaultJsonTypeInfoResolver());
options.TypeInfoResolver = options.TypeInfoResolver!.WithAddedModifier(_ => { });

JsonSerializer.Serialize(42, options);
```

Fails with the following stack overflow exception:

```
Stack overflow.
Repeated 12033 times:
--------------------------------
   at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfoResolverChain.GetTypeInfo(System.Type, System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions)
   at System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfoResolverWithAddedModifiers.GetTypeInfo(System.Type, System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions)
--------------------------------
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetTypeInfoNoCaching(System.Type)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions+CachingContext.CreateCacheEntry(System.Type, CachingContext)
   at System.Collections.Concurrent.ConcurrentDictionary`2[[System.__Canon, System.Private.CoreLib, Version=9.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e],[System.__Canon, System.Private.CoreLib, Version=9.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e]].GetOrAdd[[System.__Canon, System.Private.CoreLib, Version=9.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e]](System.__Canon, System.Func`3<System.__Canon,System.__Canon,System.__Canon>, System.__Canon)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetTypeInfoInternal(System.Type, Boolean, System.Nullable`1<Boolean>, Boolean, Boolean)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetTypeInfoForRootType(System.Type, Boolean)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.GetTypeInfo[[System.Int32, System.Private.CoreLib, Version=9.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e]](System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions)
   at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize[[System.Int32, System.Private.CoreLib, Version=9.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e]](Int32, System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions)
```

The root cause is an implicit circular dependency between resolvers that the above code induces. The `TypeInfoResolver` and `TypeInforResolverChain` properties are intended to be kept in sync: when making modifications to `TypeInfoResolverChain`, the `TypeInfoResolver` property is replaced with a new instance containing all chained resolvers. When attempting to set the `TypeInfoResolver` property, the following logic kicks in

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/da4f0a33ecec67908327138bfa0f153c3821fa78/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/JsonSerializerOptions.cs#L225-L244

Resulting in a resolver that transitively points back to itself. We should consider updating the logic so that setting `TypeInfoResolver` results in `TypeInfoResolverChain` being reset to a new instance.

First reported in https://github.com/dotnet/extensions/issues/5942#issuecomment-2671160956

review_comments: Detaching the resolver chain when a new resolver is set is an important change; please verify that downstream code properly handles a null _options reference to avoid unintended behavior.

Using a null-conditional operator here means that if the chain is detached (_options is null), the mutability check is skipped. Confirm that this behavior is intentional and that modifications on a detached chain are acceptable.
There's no longer a situation where an exception is thrown? We're not missing a test now?
It wasn't my intention to edit a test, I must have accidentally deleted it.
I assume any concurrent use of this is misuse?
Correct. No guarantees are provided while the JSO is still in edit mode.
